summary: Verified the LIVO WebRTC 'teacher writes but does not speak' fix in LiveEngine.js ontrack handler. Launched flow: nav-live → session-setup → dur-5 → session-start (microphone permission granted via context). Within 1s of connect, the DOM <audio id='livo-remote-audio'> has srcObject === MediaStream with at least one audio track (readyState='live', enabled=true), the element is NOT paused (paused=false), audio.muted=false, and the amber 'live-unlock-audio' button is NOT visible (autoplay succeeded). Connection state transitions to 'Kapcsolódás…' then 'Élő' with timer 04:59 and Hungarian transcript 'Szia Dominik!' streaming — proving the SDP exchange with OpenAI Realtime completed and the remote audio track was correctly attached (regression FIXED — previously srcObject was undefined). Transcript pull-down panel opens/closes cleanly (transcript-panel visible, transcript-close works). No JS/console errors, no page errors, no crashes. Note: the remote track shows muted=true which is a headless-browser signal (no decoded audio data), NOT a wiring bug — this is expected per agent-to-agent context.
critical_code_review_comments: LiveEngine.js ontrack handler correctly builds a MediaStream from event.track when event.streams[0] is missing (lines 94-104) and gracefully falls back to needsAudioUnlock=true when autoplay is blocked. Fix looks robust.
unlockAudio() and resumeAudio() reassert srcObject from this.remoteStream — good defensive pattern.
Minor: consider guarding a.srcObject reassignment (a.srcObject !== this.remoteStream) in ontrack to avoid restarting playback if the same stream is attached twice; currently harmless.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live audio wiring bug is fixed and verified. To reproduce: grant microphone permission on context, click nav-live → dur-5 → session-start; within 1-2s document.getElementById('livo-remote-audio').srcObject is a MediaStream with a live audio track. In headless Chromium the track.muted flag is true (no real audio data) — do NOT treat that as failure; the required DOM/WebRTC assertions per the review request all pass (hasSrcObject/isMediaStream/track live+enabled/audio not paused).
rca of the issue: Previously, in ontrack, code only used event.streams[0]; for gpt-live-1 that array can be empty so <audio> got no srcObject and no audio played though transcript events still arrived over the data channel. Fix: build a MediaStream from event.track fallback, assign to audio element, unmute + playsInline + play(), with needsAudioUnlock fallback (live-unlock-audio button) if play() promise rejects.
